compact.label: PROPOSAL A
compact.title: Compact package
compact.description: A narrower chassis and inward hip placement reduce the shoulder span. Controlled roof bevels, fine service-panel seams and recessed joint details give the body and limbs a common visual language.
changes: Hip roll axes move inward by 5 mm per side; the frame and body are repackaged around them.
Broad center panels blend into smoother end transitions. Rounded shoulder openings and fine panel seams frame the moving joints.
The nose face sits inside a continuous rounded wrap, with recessed optics. Metal caps have dark rim details and diagonal engraving.
A clean circular knee transition replaces the cosmetic inserts. The single pushrod and structural thigh halves remain accessible.
The whole limb uses a continuous taper and a shallow shin sweep, preserving motor mounts, joint centers and the single pushrod.
A wider recessed sensor face and rounded nose wrap soften the front while preserving service access and articulated shoulders.

iterations.title: First geometry pass · nominal stance
iterations.correction: Introduced the narrower package, faceted body and initial service details.
iterations.remaining: Review found tilted flat soles, square shoulder openings and an underdeveloped sensor face.

iterations.title: Rounded joints and contact soles
iterations.correction: Replaced the flat foot with a rounded sole, shaped the shoulder reliefs and added limb detailing.
iterations.remaining: The panel seams were too wide, the nose face stood proud and the knee insert ended abruptly.

iterations.title: Integrated nose · studio stance
iterations.correction: Recessed the nose panel within a continuous rim, rounded the knee insert and added cap rim detail.
iterations.remaining: A stale neutral-cover clipping boundary still left a wide seam; the final pass corrected that boundary.

iterations.title: Exterior refinement · before shin correction
iterations.correction: Fine panel seams, a seated nose face and coherent shoulder-to-knee detailing complete the exterior pass. Motion-driven motor-cover corrections are included in the final solid assembly.
iterations.remaining: The shin still bowed opposite to the studio reference. The next pass corrects that direction and the ankle transition.

iterations.title: Forward sweep · previous limb
iterations.correction: The structural shin now sweeps forward from the knee, narrows through the middle and returns toward the ankle. Its cavity, fastening bosses and surface channel follow the curve; knee and foot centers stay fixed.
iterations.remaining: The pronounced sweep and lower return made the shin visually complex and required local folding relief. The following pass simplifies the whole limb.

iterations.title: Continuous taper · limb refinement
iterations.correction: A smoother thigh transition, compact knee surround and restrained shin profile replace the deep waist and ankle return. Structural halves and their internal features are revised together.
iterations.remaining: The design is compared through sampled clearances, moving mass and section properties. Printed strength and dynamic locomotion still require physical validation.

iterations.title: Integrated nose · current body
iterations.correction: The front surround, sensor face and shoulder crown are shaped together. Rounded edges and smoother body transitions replace the sharp station breaks and projecting nose rim.
iterations.remaining: The approved limb geometry is retained. Final camera modules, seals and manufacturing tolerances still require detail design.

sculpted.label: PROPOSAL B
sculpted.title: Panelled body
sculpted.description: A curved removable body clamshell surrounds an independent motor frame. Two structural halves form each thigh and shin. Integral shin rockers and direct split bearing seats remove the separate knee head.
changes: The two shin halves directly contain the bearing seats, axial retaining shoulders and pushrod rocker. Opening the fore/aft split releases the bearings radially.
Two M4 clamps, captive nuts and compression sleeves close each shin. A recessed M8 axle bolt and outboard nut retain the removable sleeve.
The printed perpendicular motor carrier has two keyed parts with a 5 mm hip flange. The hip shroud is integral with that flange.
US hardware research prioritizes Amazon for ordinary hardware and precision suppliers for fitted parts; Lowe’s is a local fallback.
A flat 4 mm PETG electronics deck lifts on four top-access screws. A separate flat lower brace stays in the frame, and the battery cassette has independent retention.

iterations.title: First panel construction · nominal stance
iterations.correction: Built the planar/chamfered torso, service fascia, fasteners and shin channels.
iterations.remaining: Review exposed an inverted battery panel on the roof, flat tilted soles and a proud nose plate.

iterations.title: Battery panel and rounded soles
iterations.correction: Corrected the battery-panel placement, introduced rounded contact soles and added the knee-edge insert.
iterations.remaining: The nose still needed integration; shoulder framing and foot proportions remained too close to the old CAD.

iterations.title: Recessed fascia and curved detail
iterations.correction: Set the fascia into a rounded surround, corrected the cap engraving and radiused the shin-channel ends.
iterations.remaining: The following pass broadened the fascia, raised the local shoulder crowns and redesigned the rotating cowling.

iterations.title: Exterior refinement · before shin correction
iterations.correction: A wider inset face, raised shoulder crowns, real wraparound cowlings and larger rounded boots establish the final design. Rail and cowling clearances are checked in the final geometry.
iterations.remaining: The shin still bowed opposite to the studio reference. The next pass corrects that direction and the ankle transition.

iterations.title: Forward sweep · previous limb
iterations.correction: The structural shin now sweeps forward from the knee, narrows through the middle and returns toward the ankle. Its cavity, fastening bosses and surface channel follow the curve; knee and foot centers stay fixed.
iterations.remaining: The pronounced sweep and lower return made the shin visually complex and required local folding relief. The following pass simplifies the whole limb.

iterations.title: Continuous taper · limb refinement
iterations.correction: A smoother thigh transition, compact knee surround and restrained shin profile replace the deep waist and ankle return. Structural halves and their internal features are revised together.
iterations.remaining: The design is compared through sampled clearances, moving mass and section properties. Printed strength and dynamic locomotion still require physical validation.

iterations.title: Rounded body · previous face
iterations.correction: The front surround, sensor face and shoulder crown are shaped together. Rounded edges and smoother body transitions replace the sharp station breaks and projecting nose rim.
iterations.remaining: The approved limb geometry is retained. Final camera modules, seals and manufacturing tolerances still require detail design.

iterations.title: Convex face · print preparation
iterations.correction: The fascia and sensor bezel now bow together. The center roof separates from its side panels. Thigh edges are rounder and the shin keeps one shallow arc.
iterations.remaining: Unsliced plate files still need support and filament setup. Loaded performance, foot retention and final electronics interfaces remain unqualified.

iterations.title: Two-axis convex face and accessible motor cradle
iterations.correction: An independent 10 mm vertical crown adds top-to-bottom curvature while retaining the 8 mm horizontal bow. Revised roof bosses clear the panels during lifting; the battery module withdraws through a wider belly opening.
iterations.remaining: The shared tray/cassette screws require supporting the battery module during service. Wiring, final purchased components and retention details remain unqualified.

iterations.title: Integrated joints and service shell
iterations.correction: Consolidated joint components and body shells, with measured removal paths and an isolated frame view.
iterations.remaining: Frame strength, printed lip fatigue, fixed shaft retention, motor tie stacks and real wiring remain unqualified.

iterations.title: Continuous limb shells and roll openings
iterations.correction: Integrated the thigh service ring and shin walls, retained a metal knee head, and removed disappearing shoulder skins.
iterations.remaining: Open-shin torsion, printed clamp creep, bearing-lip strength and loaded locomotion remain unqualified.

iterations.title: Two-piece limbs and broad joint roots
iterations.correction: Split each shin into two structural halves, widened the fork and clamp roots, and integrated the motor face into the outer thigh.
iterations.remaining: The printed set is for unloaded fit checks. Bearing tolerances, fixed shaft retention, motor clamp hardware and load qualification remain unresolved.

iterations.title: Direct bearing seats and integrated rockers
iterations.correction: Removed the separate knee head and shoulder cover. Added two-part printed carriers and accessible axle retention.
iterations.remaining: Printed parts are unloaded prototypes. Fits, preload, exact screw engagement, roll retention, motor ties and fatigue require qualification.

iterations.title: Flat electronics deck and independent battery service
iterations.correction: Replaced the thin tray and downward ears with a flat printed deck, top screws and a fixed lower frame brace.
iterations.remaining: Actual computer standoffs, cooling, connectors and frame stiffness remain unqualified.

baseline.label: PREVIOUS CAD
baseline.title: Previous assembly
baseline.description: The preceding solid assembly, rendered from the same camera and at the same studio stance as both proposals. This isolates geometry changes from pose and framing changes.
changes: Continuous rounded torso with largely undecorated side surfaces.
Exposed cylindrical shoulder stacks and a narrow front sensor face.
Plain shin surfaces and small rounded feet.
The mechanical core provides the baseline for both proposals.
